subject: Decision criteria: latency, cost, deployment and procurement next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Decision criteria: latency/cost/SLA - Post-demo recap

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap while it’s fresh so we can align the next steps on stakeholders and procurement: 

Summary of what we heard from Finova on the call:
- Primary use case: customer support triage + real-time assistant for reps (short prompts, multi-turn chat).
- Key decision criteria: latency, per-token unit cost, deployment model (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and SLA/uptime guarantees.
- Security/legal/procurement will need SOC2 and data residency options confirmed.

Clarifying questions / what we’d like you to confirm:
1) Latency target: you mentioned needing sub-200ms p95 for the critical flow — can you confirm target (p95) for the primary path?
2) Cost: any internal $/token or monthly cost threshold we should be aware of when sizing Dedicated vs Hosted?
3) Deployment preference: is Finova inclined toward Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private (VPC/on-prem) for launch, or do you need a tradeoff analysis?
4) Procurement cadence: who owns PO/contract and what’s the expected timeline (procurement contact, legal reviewer, approval steps)?

Suggested next steps:
- If you can confirm latency and cost targets, we’ll map stakeholders and provide a short pricing + SLA matrix for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Share procurement contact or intake form (we can pre-fill standard answers).
- Propose a 30-min technical deep-dive with your engineering/security leads this week.

I’ve attached a quick datasheet with SLA and deployment summaries (redwood-datasheet.pdf).

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finova.com>, Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@finova.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Decision criteria: latency/cost/SLA - Post-demo recap

Hi Marissa —

Great summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Latency: for the customer support assistant the hard target is 150ms p95 on the primary (short-turn) flow. Non-critical batch flows can tolerate higher.
- Cost: we’re looking at an effective target below about $0.0025 / token for the majority of traffic — that will be a key part of our economic decision.
- Deployment: Preference is Dedicated if we can get predictable pricing and an SLA that satisfies ops. Private (VPC) only if Dedicated doesn’t meet our compliance needs.
- Procurement/Timing: procurement will want a 2-week review cycle once we have a draft SOW + pricing. I’m looping in procurement and Carlos (engineering) here.

Security note from our side: Maya (security) will require SOC2 Type II and encryption-at-rest; also we may have a data residency requirement for EU customers later but not for initial US rollout.

Can you share the SLA matrix and a ballpark cost comparison Dedicated vs Hosted by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Product Lead, AI
Finova
alex.johnson@finova.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision criteria: latency/cost/SLA - Post-demo recap

Thanks Alex — that helps a lot.

Quick responses: 
- We can meet 150ms p95 for the short-turn flow on Dedicated for the target throughput you described; we’ll include p50/p95/p99 numbers per model and sequence length in the SLA matrix.
- Cost: we’ll produce a side-by-side that shows your current traffic mix and estimated $/token for Hosted vs Dedicated (with committed capacity amortization).
- For security: Redwood is SOC2 Type II; we will include encryption at rest and in transit details in the security packet.

Next asks from my side: 
- Can you confirm who the economic buyer is for procurement (name & title) so we can route the commercial paperwork?
- Procurement: if you have a standard intake/PO process, can you send the template? I attached a draft mutual action plan (draft-MAP-Finova.xlsx) with proposed milestones — please review and tell me if the procurement timeline (2 weeks) is feasible.

I’ll schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive (engineering + security) for next week unless you prefer sooner.

Best,
Marissa

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finova.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 12:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Decision criteria: latency/cost/SLA - Post-demo recap

Hi Marissa / Alex —

Thanks for the loop. A couple notes from security/legal/procurement so you can include them in your packet: 
- Security requirements: SOC2 Type II report, encryption at rest & in transit, pen test summary, vendor incident response SLA, and audit log export.
- Legal: Finova standard DPA + limited redlines on liability. We will surface specific redlines after reviewing the SOW.
- Procurement: we generally issue POs and expect Net30 payment terms for initial pilot; for larger reserved commitments procurement will require a business justification and an approved budget line.

I attached our standard security intake form (Finova-security-request-form.pdf) — please complete this and return; it speeds review.

For the technical deep-dive, Carlos (engineering) can join; availability: Thurs 2-4pm ET or Fri 11-1pm ET.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Head of Security Engineering
Finova
maya.singh@finova.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@finova.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@finova.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision criteria: latency, cost, deployment and procurement next steps

Thanks Alex and Maya — quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Recap:
- Latency: Finova target 150ms p95 for the short-turn customer-support path.
- Cost: target ~ $0.0025 / token effective.
- Deployment: Finova preference is Dedicated; will escalate to Private only if compliance requires it.
- Security/Procurement: Finova needs SOC2 Type II, encryption, and the completed security intake form. Procurement expects a 2-week review for pilot paperwork, PO/Net30 for pilot.

Planned deliverables from Redwood by EOD Wed (2027-09-08):
- SLA + performance matrix (p50/p95/p99 latency by model and sequence length) for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Ballpark pricing comparison (Hosted vs Dedicated) based on the traffic mix you shared on the demo.
- Completed security packet and a pre-filled copy of Finova’s security intake form for your review.
- Draft SOW and MAP (we attached the initial MAP in the thread).

Next steps / asks from Finova:
- Alex: confirm economic buyer (name & title) and confirm procurement point of contact.
- Maya: if you can route any additional compliance checklists beyond the intake form, we’ll include those in the packet.
- Carlos / Engineering: pick a 30-min slot for a technical deep-dive (Thu 2-4pm ET or Fri 11-1pm ET suggested).

If that all looks good I’ll send calendar invites and the packet links (HubSpot record + DocuSign SOW link) once the deliverables are ready.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
